title: No AI Data Centers on Federal Lands Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Natural Resources.
summary: The No AI Data Centers on Federal Lands Act bars the creation or use of AI data centers on lands owned by the federal government. The law is intended to protect federal property, reduce environmental and security impacts, and keep large AI infrastructure out of public lands.

title: Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: The Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025 is a proposed law designed to hold companies that create and use AI systems responsible for the effects those systems have on people. It would require firms to evaluate their algorithms for bias, accuracy, and potential harms and to share those findings with the public and regulators.

title: Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on House Administration.
summary: The Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act is a proposed law designed to prevent the use of artificial intelligence to spread misinformation and manipulate public opinion during elections. It would require transparency about AI-generated content and impose penalties for deceptive or misleading use of AI in political messaging.

title: Protecting Families from AI Data Center Energy Costs Act
action: Ordered to be Reported by the Yeas and Nays: 44 - 0.
summary: The Protecting Families from AI Data Center Energy Costs Act seeks to shield households from rising utility bills that result from the massive electricity demands of AI data centers. It proposes measures such as stricter energy‑usage regulations, renewable‑energy incentives, and financial protections to keep residential energy costs stable amid the growth of AI infrastructure.

title: Homestake AI Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Energy and Natural Resources.
summary: The Homestake AI Act of 2026 is a piece of legislation that seeks to regulate the development, deployment, and use of artificial intelligence within the state of Homestake, emphasizing transparency, safety, and accountability. It establishes oversight bodies, sets data privacy and security standards, and provides guidelines for ethical AI design and application.

title: A concurrent resolution expressing the sense of Congress that the Ratepayer Protection Pledge announced on March 4, 2026, reflects sound national policy to protect ratepayers in the United States, promote electricity affordability, and ensure that all people of the United States, including households, small businesses, schools, hospitals, and farms, have access to reliable and affordable energy as artificial intelligence and data center infrastructure expands across the United States.
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Natural Resources. (text: CR S1618-1619)
summary: This resolution declares that Congress supports the Ratepayer Protection Pledge, which is designed to shield consumers from rising utility costs and promote affordable electricity. It stresses the goal of ensuring that every American—whether a household, small business, school, hospital, or farm—has access to reliable and affordable energy as AI and data‑center infrastructure grow across the country.

title: Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Environment and Public Works.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026 is a law aimed at reducing the environmental footprint of AI systems. It requires companies to assess and report the energy usage and carbon emissions of their AI models and encourages the adoption of greener hardware and renewable energy sources.

title: PROACTIV Artificial Intelligence Data Act of 2025
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The PROACTIV Artificial Intelligence Data Act of 2025 is a proposed law that sets rules for how data can be collected, stored, and used by AI systems, aiming to protect privacy and promote transparency. It requires companies to conduct impact assessments, document their data practices, and provides enforcement mechanisms to ensure compliance with these standards.

title: Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025 would require companies to regularly test and document how their automated systems impact society, ensuring fairness and transparency. It aims to give regulators the tools to review and address bias, privacy concerns, and other risks associated with algorithmic decision‑making.

title: Children's Artificial Intelligence Toy Safety Act of 2026
action: Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation. Ordered to be reported with an amendment in the nature of a substitute favorably.
summary: The Children’s Artificial Intelligence Toy Safety Act of 2026 establishes regulations to ensure that AI-powered toys sold to minors meet strict safety, privacy, and content standards. It requires manufacturers to certify that these toys do not pose physical harm, protect child data, and provide age-appropriate interactions, while providing enforcement mechanisms and penalties for non-compliance.

title: Youth AI Privacy Act
action: Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation. Ordered to be reported with an amendment in the nature of a substitute favorably.
summary: The Youth AI Privacy Act is designed to protect children’s personal information when they interact with AI systems. It establishes clear rules for data collection, consent, and usage to ensure that minors’ privacy rights are respected and safeguarded in digital environments.

title: Artificial Intelligence Physical Systems Coordination Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Physical Systems Coordination Act of 2026 establishes a national framework for the safe deployment and operation of AI‑powered physical systems, including autonomous vehicles and robots. It creates regulatory standards, oversight mechanisms, and liability guidelines to ensure accountability and public safety.

title: Expanding AI Voices Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Expanding AI Voices Act seeks to broaden the roles and influence of AI systems in public and private decision‑making. It aims to set guidelines, promote transparency, and ensure accountability as AI tools become more integral to everyday life.

title: Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act proposes a temporary halt to the construction or expansion of new data centers that are dedicated to AI operations. It aims to address environmental, economic, and security concerns by pausing new AI infrastructure projects until further study.

title: Future of Artificial Intelligence Innovation Act of 2026
action: Star Print ordered on the bill.
summary: The Future of Artificial Intelligence Innovation Act of 2026 aims to foster AI advancement by providing incentives for research and development, while establishing frameworks for ethical use and safety. It also outlines collaboration between government and industry to ensure responsible innovation and protect public interests.

title: Artificial Intelligence-Ready Data Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence-Ready Data Act seeks to set nationwide standards for gathering, labeling, and sharing data so that it is ready and reliable for AI systems to use. It establishes rules to protect privacy, enforce data quality and accessibility, and creates oversight mechanisms to ensure businesses comply.

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Evaluation Act of 2025
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Risk Evaluation Act of 2025 establishes a framework for assessing and mitigating risks associated with the development and deployment of artificial intelligence systems. The law requires companies to conduct systematic risk evaluations, report findings to regulators, and implement safety measures to protect public interests.

title: CREATE AI Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The CREATE AI Act is a proposed law that would set rules for how AI is built and used, focusing on safety and transparency. It aims to protect users by requiring companies to follow guidelines, report on risks, and keep their AI systems accountable.

title: VET Artificial Intelligence Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The VET Artificial Intelligence Act sets rules for how AI can be created and used within the VET sector, emphasizing safety, transparency, and accountability. It requires companies to assess risks, keep clear records of AI decisions, and follow regulations to protect users and stakeholders.

title: NSF AI Education Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The NSF AI Education Act of 2026 is a legislative proposal designed to expand AI education and training opportunities across K‑12 schools and higher‑education institutions. It aims to provide grants, develop curricula, and foster research collaborations to build a skilled workforce for the AI‑driven economy.

title: Small Business Artificial Intelligence Advancement Act
action: Received in the Senate and Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Small Business Artificial Intelligence Advancement Act is a proposed law that would give small companies tools and support to start using AI technology, such as training programs and financial incentives. It aims to help these businesses stay competitive and grow by making AI more accessible and affordable.

title: Small Business Artificial Intelligence Training Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Small Business Artificial Intelligence Training Act of 2026 is designed to help small businesses adopt AI by offering training programs, educational resources, and financial support. It provides grants, workshops, and tools that enable small companies to develop, implement, and manage AI solutions so they can compete more effectively in the digital economy.

title: LIFT AI Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The LIFT AI Act is a proposed law that seeks to regulate artificial intelligence by setting standards for transparency, safety, and accountability. It aims to protect users, promote responsible innovation, and ensure AI systems are trustworthy and ethically designed.

title: Artificial Intelligence Scam Prevention Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Scam Prevention Act is designed to protect consumers and businesses from fraud that leverages artificial intelligence. It outlines regulatory measures, reporting requirements, and penalties to deter the creation, deployment, and use of deceptive AI systems.

title: States' Right to Regulate AI Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The act would give individual states the authority to set their own rules and regulations around the development, use, and oversight of artificial intelligence technologies. It aims to let states address local concerns and protect residents from potential AI risks while still encouraging innovation and economic growth.

title: Artificial Intelligence Civil Rights Act of 2025
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Civil Rights Act of 2025 aims to protect individuals from discrimination and bias in AI-driven systems by enforcing fairness standards and accountability. It establishes regulations for AI developers and users to ensure transparency, explainability, and equal treatment in decision-making processes.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Critical Technology Workforce Framework Act of 2025
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence and Critical Technology Workforce Framework Act of 2025 is a proposed law that aims to create a comprehensive plan to grow and train the workforce needed to develop and use AI and other essential technologies. It seeks to ensure that the U.S. has skilled professionals, diverse talent, and a robust pipeline to support innovation, security, and economic competitiveness.

title: Artificial Intelligence Public Awareness and Education Campaign Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: This law establishes a national campaign to increase public awareness of artificial intelligence, providing education resources and guidance. It aims to ensure people understand AI's benefits and risks so they can make informed decisions and support responsible AI use.

title: TEST AI Act of 2025
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The TEST AI Act of 2025 proposes comprehensive rules to govern the development, deployment, and use of artificial intelligence technologies within the country. It emphasizes ensuring safety, transparency, accountability, and the protection of privacy and civil liberties for users and stakeholders.

title: Protection Against Foreign Adversarial Artificial Intelligence Act of 2025
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Protection Against Foreign Adversarial Artificial Intelligence Act of 2025 seeks to safeguard national security by regulating the creation and use of advanced AI systems developed by foreign adversaries. It sets requirements for testing, transparency, and export controls to prevent hostile AI from being deployed in ways that could threaten U.S. interests.

title: SBA Artificial Intelligence Utilization Act of 2026
action: Received in the Senate and Read twice and referred to the Committee on Small Business and Entrepreneurship.
summary: The SBA Artificial Intelligence Utilization Act of 2026 is a federal law that encourages small businesses to adopt and use AI technologies while setting basic safety and privacy standards. It provides guidance, funding, and oversight to help small firms integrate AI tools responsibly and stay competitive.

title: Self-Improving AI Monitoring Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.
summary: The Self‑Improving AI Monitoring Act requires developers of AI systems that can autonomously improve to report their upgrades and performance metrics to a regulatory body. It establishes oversight procedures to ensure that such self‑learning systems operate safely, transparently, and in compliance with established ethical and legal standards.

title: Generative AI Terrorism Risk Assessment Act
action: Received in the Senate and Read twice and referred to the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs.
summary: The Generative AI Terrorism Risk Assessment Act is a proposed law that would require AI developers and providers to evaluate how their generative models could be used to support terrorism. It aims to identify, monitor, and mitigate any potential risks that AI tools might pose to national security and public safety.

title: Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: This act addresses the environmental effects of artificial intelligence systems, setting guidelines to reduce energy usage and carbon emissions. It establishes reporting requirements for AI developers and promotes sustainable practices throughout the AI lifecycle.

title: Doctors Not AI Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on Ways and Means, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Doctors Not AI Act of 2026 is a U.S. law that bans the use of artificial intelligence for diagnosing and treating patients without a licensed physician’s direct oversight. It requires that all AI medical tools be FDA‑approved and mandates that a human doctor must always participate in the decision‑making process.

title: Full AI Stack Export Promotion Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute by the Yeas and Nays: 37 - 7.
summary: The Full AI Stack Export Promotion Act aims to boost the export of comprehensive AI technologies, from hardware and software to end‑user services, ensuring U.S. companies remain competitive worldwide. It proposes incentives, regulatory streamlining, and support mechanisms for firms involved in the entire AI ecosystem to facilitate international sales and partnerships.

title: Open-Source AI Leadership Act
action: Forwarded by Subcommittee to Full Committee by Voice Vote.
summary: The Open‑Source AI Leadership Act aims to promote the creation and widespread use of open‑source AI technologies by setting out guidelines, providing funding, and encouraging collaboration among developers, companies, and researchers. By fostering transparency and shared innovation, it intends to position the United States as a global leader in responsible, accessible AI development.

title: Responsible Artificial Intelligence for Veterans Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
summary: The Responsible Artificial Intelligence for Veterans Act of 2026 aims to ensure that AI technologies used in veteran services are developed and deployed responsibly, protecting veterans' privacy, security, and well‑being. It establishes guidelines, oversight, and accountability mechanisms to promote ethical AI practices in programs that serve military veterans.

title: Advanced AI Security Readiness Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Intelligence (Permanent Select).
summary: The Advanced AI Security Readiness Act is a piece of legislation aimed at strengthening the protection of AI systems against potential risks and threats. It mandates that organizations implement robust security measures, conduct thorough risk assessments, and report incidents to a designated national authority to ensure safer AI deployment.

title: Eliminating Bias in Algorithmic Systems Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform.
summary: The Eliminating Bias in Algorithmic Systems Act of 2026 seeks to reduce unfair bias in AI and automated decision systems by requiring companies to audit their algorithms, provide transparency about data and model design, and enforce penalties for discriminatory outcomes. The law also establishes a federal oversight body that will set guidelines, certify compliant systems, and support research into bias‑mitigation techniques.
